# DiscoPoP B19 and B18 — a wrong `lastprivate` in three places and the Do-All that nests with counters declared at the top of the function had lost: the repairs and their regression check

*Generated by `agent/tools/campaign.py reports` from `results/campaign.json` and the experiment record (`agent/THESIS_EXPERIMENTS.md`). Edit those, then regenerate — not this file.*

**Status:** done

## The question

After the explorer's repairs of 8 Oct (a last value assigned in only some passes blocks Do-All; an array is shared; only a loop's own units decide its clauses; a write-after-read is attached to units by its own roles): does DiscoPoP alone give every one of the 44 tsvc_c3 packages its measured class, with a difference only where the repairs aim (s331, s481), and what does it now say on the 31 packages outside TSVC?

## Result in one paragraph

Passed on TSVC: on the 44 tsvc_c3 packages every class and every draw is as before the repairs; DiscoPoP offers other directives on the two loops the repairs aim at and nowhere else (s331: nothing offered any more; s481: the kept directive without lastprivate(nl)). Outside TSVC, correlation, covariance and fdtd-2d have their outer loop's directive back in 3 of 3 draws (5.7×, 5.5×, 4.1×) — nine loops given back by the B18 repair, none lost. Two things the draws showed that are not the repairs': on PolyBench the explorer, on one profile, blocks every loop that carries an observed dependence or none of them, never a part, and blocks none in 57 of 81 profiles (B21, measured, not traced) — gramschmidt's loop comes back only in such draws (2 of 3); and a rule of DiscoPoP's own calls a loop parallel whose pass reads an array element a later pass overwrites (B22, new: adi's last nest, refused by the gate in 3 of 3 draws; on TSVC hidden by B16). No model in any of it.

The server's draws are registered with this row and launched after it; no model is involved.** **B19 — three mechanisms, three repairs** (`pattern_detectors/new_do_all_detector.py`; `discopop_agent/docs/DISCOPOP_BUG_REPORTS.md` has the detail). (1) *A last value assigned in only some passes* (`s331`): the detector's modelled iterations cannot tell a conditional assignment from one every pass makes; the control flow can — with the assigning units taken out, a pass must not get from its first unit back to it. Such a loop is no longer reported Do-All (DiscoPoP has no clause for "the last assignment"); the record it leaves is the write-after-write between passes on the assignment's line, marked observed where the profile holds the assignment overwriting itself. Only a loop that would otherwise be reported is concerned. (2) *Arrays:* the test that keeps a pointer's target `shared` looked for `*` or `&` in the type; `real_t[32000]` has neither. An array is now `shared` on the loop that fills it and on the one that reads it. (3) *`s481`:* with `exit(0)` in the inner loop's body the task graph puts units of the loop around it into the inner loop's iterations; a loop's clauses are now decided by its own units and what they call. The modelling defect itself is B20. **B18 — traced:** the explorer of the commit before B10's fix (`9a86f4855`) and the explorer of that fix (`8c7e6066f`) on ONE kept profile of `polybench/correlation`: before, the loops at lines 98, 106, 109 are Do-All with their inner counters private; after, blocked on a static RAW on the counter. So the change that took the Do-All away is B10's fix — ours — and the reason is older code it met: `PEGraphX.from_parsed_input` attaches a write-after-read to the units of its lines by a read-after-write's roles, so on a one-line `for (j = 0; j < m; j++)` the unit that only initialises `j` is credited with the condition's and the increment's reads; B10's rule (a read and a write of one variable on one line in one unit: read first) then makes the counter read-first, and it is no longer privatizable. **Repaired** in `classes/PEGraph/PEGraphX.py`: a write-after-read is attached by its own roles; where a line has no unit in the right role the old lookup stays. On the kept profile, three runs of each explorer: the three loops Do-All in 0 of 3 before and 3 of 3 after. B10's own check passes unchanged. The B18 entry's sentence that no TSVC package is affected stands as an observation only (TSVC declares its counters in the loop header). **Verified on the Mac, on the final code:** the agent's feature suite — 67 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped; the new check `b19-last-value` (a 40-line program holding all of B19's places and B18's nest) fails on the explorer before the repairs on five counts and passes after. DiscoPoP's end-to-end tests — 35 of 35; the three new cases (`last_private/case_2`, `shared/case_4`, `private/case_2`) fail on the explorer before the repairs (the conditional loop reported; `last_private(Arr)`; the nest's outer loop not reported) and pass after. mypy and `black --check` on the explorer clean. The 44 `tsvc_c3` packages, one kept profile each, the explorer before against the one after: 42 packages with the same patterns, clauses and blocked loops; the two that differ are `s331` (the search loop no longer reported, its record a write-after-write on `j`) and `s481` (the inner loop's directive without the clause). **Found on the way.** *B20:* a call that does not return (`exit`) in the body of a nested loop loses every dependence the surrounding loop carries — that loop is reported Do-All (a 20-line reproducer; `s481`'s repetition loop, on the Mac's profile and in the server's draw `t0_11_c3_a`, where the gate refused the directive under ThreadSanitizer). *B21:* the explorer's verdict still differs between runs on one profile (`correlation`, three runs, before and after the repairs alike: two accumulation loops and the two output loops Do-All in two runs, blocked on their true dependence in one) — B4's symptom on a program with several nests; the TSVC packages do not show it.
